headline: Nature Medicine has published a collection of articles saying clinical AI must prove itself in real hospitals and clinics, with several trials finding no clear gain.
score_reason: Authoritative journal, but a collection page summarising many papers, not one new finding.
importance_line: It tells doctors, hospitals and regulators that AI tools that score well in tests can fall short in real care, though we only saw one-line summaries of each paper.
summary: Nature Medicine's new collection on real-world clinical AI says success depends on workflow, human-AI collaboration and trust as well as the algorithm. Its summaries include a Kenyan primary-care trial where ChatGPT-4o decision support did not significantly cut 14-day treatment failure and a breast screening trial where AI triage was not noninferior to standard double reading.
notes: Collection landing page with summaries, not the papers themselves; dates of individual papers not stated.
